Chapter 9: Personal Transformation—Lessons Learned in the Hermit Kingdom
Living in North Korea—it's something that changes you, sometimes in ways you never expected.
At first, it feels like stepping into a completely different world. Everything is new—the language, the customs, and that constant sense of being watched. It can feel overwhelming, almost like you’re carrying a weight you can’t quite put down.
But as days turn into weeks, and weeks into months, those differences start to blend into the background. What really stands out aren't the rules or the restrictions, but the moments when you truly connect with others. Maybe it’s a shared meal, a quiet conversation, or a simple act of kindness that breaks through the barriers.
Think about this: one foreigner, looking back on his journey, realized just how much he’d changed. Patience—something he’d always struggled with—became almost automatic. He learned to listen, to adapt, and to see things from someone else’s perspective. Those skills, picked up out of necessity, ended up becoming part of who he was, long after he left.
Of course, it’s not all smooth sailing. There are moments when the isolation feels like too much, or when the challenges seem endless. But those tough times? They’re balanced out by a growing sense of resilience. Living and working in North Korea tests your character—it teaches you humility, and a deep sense of empathy.
When it’s finally time to leave, the feeling is bittersweet. There’s relief, sure—getting back to freedom, family, and the comforts of home. But there’s also this unexpected sense of loss. The friendships you’ve built, the lessons you’ve learned, and those small victories—they stick with you, shaping how you see everything going forward.
For anyone who’s spent time in North Korea, that experience never really fades into the background. It colors every conversation, every decision, and even the hopes you carry for the future.
So, what’s the biggest lesson? Sometimes, in the most unlikely places, you find real connection, meaning, and hope. And those things—they stay with you, no matter where life takes you next.
